examples.en: Food got stuck and I nearly choked.
The doctor opened the patient's airway.

examples.ko: 월급이 들어와서 이번 달은 숨통이 좀 트였어요.
examples.en: My pay came in, so I have some breathing room this month.

examples.ko: 일이 너무 많아서 잠깐 쉬며 숨통을 틔웠어요.
examples.en: I had so much work that I took a short break to catch my breath.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 경쟁사 때문에 숨통이 조여 오고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is being squeezed hard by its competitor.
When I opened the window, I felt I could breathe again.

explain: 숨통은 숨 쉬는 길인데, '숨통이 트이다', '숨통을 조이다'처럼 비유로도 많이 써요. 의학에서는 '기관'이나 '기도'라고 해요.

phrases.en: to finally get some breathing room
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들고 답답하던 상황이 풀려서 한숨 돌릴 때 써요. 돈, 일, 시간 모두에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tight or stressful situation eases and you can finally relax a bit. It works for money, work, or time.

explain_en: 숨통 is the passage for breathing, and it is also widely used figuratively, as in 숨통이 트이다 or 숨통을 조이다. In medicine the terms are 기관 or 기도.

en: to go blind; to lose one's sight

examples.en: My grandfather hurt his eyes in an accident and lost his sight.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 때 병에 걸려 실명했어요.
examples.en: He caught an illness as a child and went blind.

examples.ko: 실명할 위험이 있어서 병원에 서둘러 갔어요.
examples.en: There was a risk of going blind, so I hurried to the hospital.
Even after losing his sight, he kept making music.
I hear that if you lose sight in one eye, your sense of distance changes.

examples.ko: 실명하지 않으려면 눈 검사를 자주 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid going blind, you should get your eyes checked often.

explain: 실명하다는 눈이 보이지 않게 되는 일을 조심스럽게 말하는 말이에요. '눈이 멀다'는 직접적이라 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. 시력이 일부 떨어질 때는 '시력을 잃다', '시력이 나빠지다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그분은 사고로 실명한 뒤 음악을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: After going blind in an accident, he started music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미거나 '실명한 뒤'처럼 때를 나타낼 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form that modifies a following noun or marks timing, as in 실명한 뒤 ('after going blind').

phrases.en: My grandmother lost her sight due to an illness.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실명하다'와 비슷하고 더 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 실명하다 but easier.

phrases.example: 공사 중에 눈을 다쳐서 실명할 뻔했어요.
phrases.en: I hurt my eye during construction and almost went blind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 그러지는 않았지만 위험했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it nearly happened but didn't.

explain_en: 실명하다 is the careful way to say someone's eyes stopped seeing. '눈이 멀다' is blunt, so avoid it for people. When sight only weakens, say '시력을 잃다' or '시력이 나빠지다'.

examples.ko: 약손가락으로 눈 주위를 살살 두드려 크림을 발라요.
examples.en: I apply cream by gently tapping around my eyes with my ring finger.

examples.ko: 약손가락이 잘 안 펴져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My ring finger wouldn't straighten, so I went to the hospital.
It's hard for me to move just my ring finger on its own.
Yesterday I got my ring finger caught in a door and hurt it.

examples.ko: 약손가락에 낀 반지가 너무 꽉 껴요.
examples.en: The ring on my ring finger is too tight.
I got a small cut on the tip of my ring finger.

explain: '약지'와 같은 손가락이에요. 한자어 '약지'는 설명문이나 병원에서 자주 보이고, 말할 때는 '약손가락'이 더 편하게 들려요. 엄지, 검지, 중지, 약지, 새끼손가락 순서로 불러요.

phrases.en: I put a ring on my ring finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한자어 이름이고 설명문이나 병원에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The Sino-Korean name, common in explanations and at hospitals.

phrases.en: I hurt my ring finger by getting it caught in the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손가락을 다쳤을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a finger gets injured.

phrases.en: Try opening your ring finger and little finger together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옆에 있는 손가락과 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when naming it with the neighboring finger.

explain_en: It is the same finger as '약지'. The Sino-Korean '약지' shows up in explanations and at the hospital, while '약손가락' sounds more natural in speech. The fingers go: 엄지, 검지, 중지, 약지, 새끼손가락.

t90.ax: The ring on my ring finger is too tight.

en: to drown; to submerge and die

examples.ko: 작은 배가 뒤집혀서 두 명이 익사했어요.
examples.en: A small boat capsized and two people drowned.
I am afraid of water and worry that I might drown.

examples.ko: 수영을 못하는 사람은 깊은 물에서 익사하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: People who cannot swim easily drown in deep water.

examples.ko: 바다에서 익사하는 사고는 파도가 높을 때 많아요.
examples.en: Drownings at sea happen often when the waves are high.
He drowned before the rescue team arrived.
In the movie, the hero saves a drowning person.

explain: '물에 빠지다'는 살 수도 있지만 '익사하다'는 물에 빠져 목숨을 잃었다는 뜻이라 뉴스와 사고 기사에서 써요. 가까운 사람의 일을 말할 때는 보통 '사고로 돌아가셨다'처럼 돌려 말해요.

phrases.en: I almost drowned in the sea when I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 죽지는 않았지만 거의 그럴 뻔했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it almost happened but did not.

phrases.en: Wear a life jacket so that you do not drown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 익사를 막기 위한 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the purpose of avoiding drowning.

phrases.en: That person fell into the river and died.
phrases.nuance_ko: '익사하다'를 풀어서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer way of saying 'to drown'.
phrases.en_equiv: to die by falling in water

explain_en: '물에 빠지다' can end with survival, but '익사하다' means someone died in the water, so it appears in news and accident reports. For someone close, people usually soften it with '사고로 돌아가셨다'.

examples.en: The doctor admitted the patient right away.

examples.ko: 부모님이 열이 높은 아이를 입원시키기로 했어요.
examples.en: The parents decided to hospitalize the child with a high fever.
The hospital admits you if your condition is serious.
His family said they had to get him admitted.

examples.ko: 할아버지를 입원시킨 뒤에 매일 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: After getting my grandfather admitted, I went to the hospital every day.

examples.ko: 입원시키지 않고 집에서 치료할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: You can also treat them at home without admitting them.

explain: '입원하다'는 자기가 병원에 들어가는 것이고, '입원시키다'는 다른 사람을 입원하게 하는 것이에요. 반대되는 말은 '퇴원하다', '퇴원시키다'예요. 주어는 보통 의사나 가족처럼 입원을 정하는 사람이에요.

phrases.en: The child is very sick, so we have to hospitalize him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어야 하다'와 함께 입원이 필요하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -아/어야 하다 to say hospitalization is needed.

phrases.en: My father was admitted to the hospital last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 병원에 들어가는 것이라서, 주어가 환자예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The patient himself enters the hospital, so the patient is the subject.

phrases.en: The hospital discharged the patient today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입원시키다'의 반대로, 다른 사람을 병원에서 나가게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 입원시키다; sends someone out of the hospital.

explain_en: '입원하다' is entering the hospital yourself; '입원시키다' is making someone else get admitted. The opposites are '퇴원하다' and '퇴원시키다'. The subject is usually someone who decides on the admission, such as a doctor or family member.

examples.en: I burned the roof of my mouth on hot pizza.
The roof of my mouth is scraped and it hurts.
Touch your tongue to the roof of your mouth.
A peanut skin is stuck to the roof of my mouth.
The skin on my palate peeled off, so I can't eat anything.
At the dentist they even checked the roof of my mouth carefully.

explain: '입천장을 데다', '입천장이 까지다/벗겨지다'처럼 뜨거운 음식을 먹고 다쳤을 때 특히 자주 써요. 의학에서는 '구개'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The roof of my mouth got scraped after eating hot soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까지다'와 비슷하게 뜨거운 음식 때문에 다쳤을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 'to get scraped', used when hot food hurts the mouth.

phrases.en: The rice cake is stuck to the roof of my mouth, so it's hard to talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈적한 음식을 먹을 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when eating sticky food.

phrases.en: My palate hurts after eating snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱한 음식이나 상처로 아플 때 간단히 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple way to say it hurts, from hard food or a sore.

explain_en: It is used most often when you hurt it on hot food, as in '입천장을 데다' or '입천장이 까지다/벗겨지다'. The medical term is '구개'.

examples.en: At the factory they cut steel plates with a machine.
The firefighter cut through the door and saved the person.

examples.ko: 파이프를 절단할 때는 보호 안경을 써요.
examples.en: I wear safety glasses when cutting pipe.

examples.ko: 두꺼운 나무를 절단하는 데 시간이 꽤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes quite a while to cut thick wood.

examples.ko: 의사는 어쩔 수 없이 다리를 절단했어요.
examples.en: The doctor had no choice but to amputate the leg.
I brought the board cut to the right length.

explain: 절단하다는 단단한 것을 완전히 끊거나 몸의 일부를 잘라 낼 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 음식이나 종이에는 '자르다'를 써야 자연스러워요. 쓰기는 '~을/를 절단하다'예요.

phrases.en: I cut the paper with scissors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 종이 같은 일상적인 것에 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday word for food, paper, and the like.

phrases.en: Please cut this wire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사나 작업 현장에서 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make a request at a work site.

phrases.example: 이 칼로는 철을 절단할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: You can't cut iron with this knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단한 것을 자를 수 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something hard can't be cut.

explain_en: 절단하다 is a stiff word for cutting something hard all the way through or amputating a body part. For food or paper, '자르다' sounds natural. The pattern is '~을/를 절단하다'.

t90.ax: I wear safety glasses when cutting pipe.

examples.ko: 다친 손을 깨끗한 천으로 눌러 지혈했어요.
examples.en: I pressed the injured hand with a clean cloth to stop the bleeding.
When your nose bleeds, you lower your head and stop the bleeding.
The doctor first stopped the bleeding and then stitched the wound.
If you don't stop the bleeding, the blood keeps coming.
I learned how to stop bleeding by tying with a strap.

examples.ko: 빨리 지혈해야 해서 구급대원이 붕대를 감았어요.
examples.en: The paramedic wrapped a bandage because the bleeding had to be stopped quickly.

explain: '피를 멈추다'보다 응급 상황에서 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요. 상처를 누르거나 감싸서 피를 멈추게 하는 행동에 쓰고, 약으로 멈추는 것은 '지혈제'를 쓴다고 해요. 응급처치 교육에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 의사 선생님, 이 상처 좀 지혈해 주세요.
phrases.en: Doctor, please stop the bleeding on this wound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 부탁하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request for someone else to do it.

phrases.en: I learned how to stop bleeding at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응급처치 교육에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in first-aid lessons.

phrases.en: I pressed for a long time but the bleeding won't stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피가 멈추지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the bleeding does not stop.

explain_en: It sounds far more natural in an emergency than '피를 멈추다'. It is used for pressing or wrapping a wound to stop blood, and a medicine for this is called '지혈제'. It comes up often in first aid training.

examples.en: He suffered a fatal injury in a traffic accident.
Thankfully, they say it is not a fatal wound.
It is not life-threatening, so a few days of rest is enough.

examples.ko: 이번 실수는 우리 회사에 치명상이 되었어요.
examples.en: This mistake was a fatal blow to our company.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 치명상을 입고도 끝까지 달렸어요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie kept running to the end despite a fatal wound.

examples.ko: 가슴에 입은 치명상 때문에 병원에 실려 갔어요.
examples.en: He was carried to the hospital because of a mortal wound in the chest.

explain: 보통 '치명상을 입다'로 써요. 목숨이 위험한 상처라서 가벼운 상처에는 쓰지 않아요. 가벼운 상처는 '경상', 심한 상처는 '중상'이라고 해요. 회사나 계획이 크게 망가질 때도 비유로 '치명상'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: He suffered a fatal wound in the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상처를 받은 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase, used when the injured person is the subject.

phrases.en: That accident gave the player a fatal injury.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입다'와 달리 다른 사람에게 상처를 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 입다, it means causing the wound to someone else.

phrases.en: This mistake became a fatal blow to the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 망가지는 일을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for something that does great damage.

explain_en: It is usually '치명상을 입다'. Because it means a life-threatening wound, it is not used for minor ones: a light injury is '경상' and a serious one is '중상'. It is also used figuratively when a company or plan is badly damaged.

examples.en: I wore skull makeup on Halloween.
I saw an old skull at the museum.

examples.ko: 해골 모양 반지는 저한테 안 어울려요.
examples.en: A skull-shaped ring does not suit me.
I was startled when a skeleton suddenly appeared in the movie.

examples.ko: 독이 있다는 표시로 해골 그림을 붙여요.
examples.en: They put a skull picture to show something is poisonous.

examples.ko: 며칠 못 자서 얼굴이 해골 같아요.
examples.en: I could not sleep for days, so my face looks like a skull.

explain: '뼈'는 몸속의 뼈 하나하나이고, '해골'은 죽은 사람이나 동물의 머리뼈, 또는 뼈대 전체예요. 장난스럽게 '얼굴이 해골 같다'고 하면 많이 말랐다는 뜻이에요. 무서운 분위기의 말이라서 격식 있는 자리에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: The children are eating skull-shaped candy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 해골처럼 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an object is shaped like a skull.

phrases.en: There is a skull drawing on the flag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그려진 해골을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a drawn or printed skull.

phrases.en: Your face looks like a skull these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 마른 모습을 장난스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful way to say someone is very thin.

explain_en: '뼈' is each bone in the body, while '해골' is the skull or the whole skeleton of a dead person or animal. Jokingly saying '얼굴이 해골 같다' means someone looks very thin. It has a creepy feel, so it is rarely used in formal settings.

t90.ax: I wore skull makeup on Halloween.

examples.en: I strained a tendon in my ankle while exercising.

examples.ko: 목에 힘줄이 보일 정도로 크게 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: He shouted so loudly that the sinews in his neck showed.
This meat has a lot of sinew, so it is tough.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 무릎 힘줄 수술을 받았어요.
examples.en: That player had knee tendon surgery.

examples.ko: 팔에 힘줄이 튀어나올 만큼 열심히 운동했어요.
examples.en: I worked out so hard that the tendons stood out on my arms.
Beef sinew becomes tender if you boil it for a long time.

explain: 몸에서는 '힘줄이 끊어지다'처럼 다친 이야기에, 음식에서는 '힘줄이 질기다'처럼 고기 이야기에 써요. '근육'은 움직이는 살이고, 힘줄은 그 근육을 뼈에 붙여 주는 줄이에요.

phrases.en: The tendon in my ankle snapped while I was playing soccer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 다친 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about a serious injury.

phrases.example: 이 고기는 힘줄이 질겨서 먹기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: The tendon in this meat is tough, so it's hard to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 먹을 때 질긴 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the tough part when eating meat.

phrases.example: 무거운 짐을 들다가 손목 힘줄을 다쳤어요.
phrases.en: I hurt the tendon in my wrist while lifting a heavy load.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다치다'는 앞에 '을/를'을 붙여 다친 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 다치다, use 을/를 to name the injured part.

explain_en: For the body it appears in injuries, like 힘줄이 끊어지다, and for food in meat talk, like 힘줄이 질기다. 근육 is the muscle that moves, while 힘줄 is the cord that attaches a muscle to bone.

examples.en: In summer, we rode a rubber boat in the valley.
The kids are having fun on the rubber boat.

examples.ko: 고무보트에 바람을 넣는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to pump air into the rubber boat.

examples.ko: 파도가 센 날에는 고무보트를 타면 위험해요.
examples.en: Riding a rubber boat on a day with strong waves is dangerous.
The rescue team saved people using a rubber boat.

examples.ko: 고무보트는 가벼워서 혼자서도 옮길 수 있어요.
examples.en: A rubber boat is light, so you can carry it by yourself.

explain: 사람이 안에 앉아서 타는 배라서 몸에 끼는 '튜브'와는 달라요. 바람을 넣어 쓰기 때문에 '바람을 넣다, 타다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: I'm going to ride a rubber boat on the river this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 이용하는 활동을 말할 때 '타다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 타다 for riding the boat.

phrases.example: 고무보트에 바람을 넣는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: It took a long time to inflate the rubber boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용하기 전에 공기를 채우는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Filling it with air before use.

phrases.en: The kids launched the rubber boat on the lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 물 위에 놓는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes setting the boat on the water.

explain_en: You sit inside it like a boat, so it differs from a '튜브' that you wear around your body. It is inflated, so it goes with '바람을 넣다' and '타다'.

examples.en: It suddenly poured on my way home.

examples.ko: 늦은 밤 혼자 걷는 귀갓길이 무서워요.
examples.en: The walk home alone late at night is scary.
The subway on the way home is always crowded.
The route home in front of the school has been made safe.
They patrol for the children's safe walk home.
Walking with a friend makes even the way home enjoyable.

explain: '퇴근길'은 일을 마치고, '하굣길'은 학교를 마치고 가는 길인데, 귀갓길은 어디서든 집으로 돌아가는 길이라 더 넓게 써요. 밤길 안전 이야기에서 특히 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: On my way home, I stopped by a convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 집에 가는 도중이라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에 means during the trip home.

phrases.en: The way home is dangerous at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤길 안전 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in talk about night-time safety.

phrases.example: 귀갓길 안전을 위해 친구와 같이 가요.
phrases.en: For safety on the way home, I go with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 뉴스에서 명사처럼 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun phrase in notices and news.

explain_en: '퇴근길' is the way home after work and '하굣길' after school, but 귀갓길 covers going home from anywhere. It is often heard in talk about safety on night streets.

examples.ko: 급정거 때문에 뒷좌석에 둔 짐이 앞으로 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: Because of the sudden stop, the bags on the back seat spilled forward.

examples.ko: 아이가 갑자기 뛰어나온 탓에 급정거가 불가피했어요.
examples.en: A child suddenly ran out, so a sudden stop was unavoidable.
The bus stopped suddenly and the passengers staggered.

examples.ko: 택시가 갑자기 급정거하는 바람에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The taxi suddenly braked hard and I was startled.

examples.ko: 앞차가 급정거할 때를 대비해서 거리를 두세요.
examples.en: Keep your distance in case the car ahead stops suddenly.

examples.ko: 그 차가 급정거했지만 늦어서 가볍게 부딪혔어요.
examples.en: That car braked hard but too late, and they bumped lightly.

explain: 자동차나 버스가 갑자기 서는 상황에 써요. '급정차'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 급브레이크를 밟아 확 서는 장면에 잘 어울려요. 사람이 갑자기 멈출 때는 '갑자기 멈춰 서다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The car in front suddenly stopped.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급정거하다'의 해요체 과거형이라 일어난 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form, used to tell what happened.

phrases.en: The bus stopped suddenly, so I almost fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하며 문장을 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give a reason and connect sentences.

phrases.en: I saw a child and slammed on the brakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급정거'가 일어나게 한 행동을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action that causes a sudden stop.

explain_en: It is used when a car or bus stops suddenly. It is almost the same as '급정차' and fits scenes of slamming the brakes. When a person stops abruptly, say '갑자기 멈춰 서다'.
